title: From Egypt Lately Freed
description: From Egypt Lately Freed in Tonic Solfa to FRANCONIA, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 42, “The Pilgrim' song”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to FRANCONIA; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: From E-gypt late-ly freed By the Re-deem-er's grace; A rough and thor-ny path we tread, In hopes to see his face.

lines: A rough and thorny path we tread,
In hopes to see his face.
This only leads to endless day,
There we shall have unclouded skies,
Here griefs, and cares, and pains,
And we shall weep no more.
The joy, prepared for suff'ring saints,

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to FRANCONIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
